title: Least Consecutive Pair of Primitive Roots
summary: Let $p>1$ be a large prime number and let $x=O((\log p)^2(\log\log p)^5$ be a real number. It is proved that the least consecutive pair of primitive roots $u\ne\pm1, v^2$ and $u+1$ satisfies the upper bound $u\ll x$ in the prime field $\mathbb{F}_p$.
